items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: Mark Copeland was playing piano and Peacock was, it was Mark’s record, and Peacock was playing bass and we were playing a blues

ctx.x: I’ve always been fascinated by the challenge of hearing I guess what you would call alternate chord changes. If your organist decides to start some new substitutions that you haven’t heard before, how do you nail those? Or do you?

Well some of them you just hear. I mean some of them might be more things you would expect, I mean just kind of substitutions that occur a lot. He generally, he won’t go too far away from what we play. I mean he won’t play things that I’ll never hear, unless we’re improvising really freely and then you don’t try to nail anything, and then the whole idea is not to really nail anything but just to sort of kind of play, it’s like playing alone together. You can be playing together but you might have your own…
Just recently, no I’m sorry, this is 1986, you said, “Playing what you hear is the greatest challenge.”
